fields.h1: Build Prior Authorization Automation for Your Practice
fields.hero_description: Build prior authorization automation that tracks each request, flags late decisions, and starts renewals before visits run out.
fields.features_heading: What Your Prior Authorization Tracker Handles
fields.features_subheading: The tracker sits between your practice and each payer and keeps the full record of every request in one place.
fields.feature_1:
A document checklist for each payer

List what each payer asks for by service, such as an office note or an imaging report. A request stays held until its checklist is complete, and the app names what is missing.
fields.feature_2:
Rules described in plain sentences

Describe how requests move, who works each one, and when a late one escalates. Emergent builds the tracker, its database, and the logic, and another prompt changes a rule.
fields.feature_3:
Faxed and scanned letters read into fields

Upload a payer's decision letter, and AI reads the decision, the approved visits, and the authorization number into the request. A low-confidence value waits for a person.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts that carry a number, not a chart

A late request sends its coordinator an alert in Slack, by email, or in the app with the request number and a link. No patient details ever travel inside the alert itself.
fields.feature_5:
Connected to the systems you run today

The app connects to your scheduling or billing system through its API, so a new order arrives as a request. Every request, letter, and decision is saved in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
Your tracker's code in your GitHub

Export the full code of the tracker to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Your IT team can read how requests are stored and who can open them before the app goes live.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Requests at One Orthopedic Practice
fields.tab_content_1:
Held until all four documents are attached

Request PA-4127 for a lumbar MRI comes in from the scheduling system at Calderbank Orthopedics. Pelrose Health Plan's checklist for that service asks for 4 documents, and 3 are attached. The office visit note is missing, so the app marks the request Not ready to send and assigns it to Ophira Grausam.
fields.tab_content_2:
The approval letter fills four fields in the record

Pelrose's decision on PA-4098 arrives as a scanned letter. The app reads four fields: the decision, 12 approved physical therapy visits, a 90-day approval window, and the authorization number. That number reads at low confidence, and Halvard Wieczorek checks it against the letter before the record is saved.
fields.tab_content_3:
Ophira hears on day 3 when the payer is silent

Request PA-4133 went to Pelrose on a Tuesday, and Calderbank gives each standard request 3 business days before a coordinator follows up. By Friday there is still no decision. The app marks PA-4133 late and sends Ophira a Slack direct message that says only that the request needs action, with an Open request button.
fields.tab_content_4:
Renewal starts when 2 of 12 visits remain

Approval PA-4098 covers 12 physical therapy visits, and 10 are used. Calderbank's rule opens a renewal task when 2 visits remain, which leaves room to send a new request before the last visit. The app emails Ophira a link to the task, and the renewal starts with the first request's documents attached.

fields.hero_prompt: Build prior authorization automation for my orthopedic practice that tracks each payer request and flags late decisions.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up prior authorization automation?

plan.angle: The top 10 are vendor pages and explainers selling AI agents that phone payers and fill portals for hospitals; none shows the tracker a practice runs itself. This page shows four working screens at one orthopedic practice: a request held until every document on the payer's checklist is attached, a scanned approval letter read into the record, a request with no decision after 3 business days that messages the coordinator, and an approval with 2 visits left that opens a renewal. Alerts carry only a request number and a link, and the FAQ quotes CMS and HealthCare.gov exactly.
tab_stories: Calderbank Orthopedics logs request PA-4127 for a lumbar MRI; Pelrose Health Plan's checklist for the service asks for 4 documents, 3 are attached, so the app holds the request in Ophira Grausam's queue until the office visit note is added.

Pelrose's approval letter for request PA-4098 arrives as a scanned PDF; the app reads the decision, the 12 approved physical therapy visits and the authorization number into the record, and the authorization number reads at 61% confidence so Halvard Wieczorek checks it before it is saved.

Request PA-4133 has no decision 3 business days after it went to the payer; the app marks it late and sends Ophira Grausam a Slack direct message that says only that the request needs action, with an Open request button.
Approval PA-4098 covers 12 physical therapy visits and 10 are used; at 2 visits left the app opens a renewal task and emails Ophira Grausam a link to it.

claims_to_source: Preauthorization is a decision by a health insurer or plan that a health care service, treatment plan, prescription drug or durable medical equipment is medically necessary
Preauthorization is sometimes called prior authorization, prior approval or precertification
CMS requires impacted payers, excluding QHP issuers on the FFEs, to send prior authorization decisions within 72 hours for expedited requests and seven calendar days for standard requests
Impacted payers must provide a specific reason for denied prior authorization decisions, beginning in 2026
The Prior Authorization API must communicate whether the payer approves, denies or requests more information, and must be implemented beginning January 1, 2027
Medicare Advantage organizations are among the impacted payers under CMS-0057-F
